summary: The explicit data/errorlevel=1/fresh-directory extractall policy is supported. Four material release/path/comparison/phase defects prevent a full PASS; all consequential final claims and six obligations have been independently checked against primary facts.

axes.label: all required brief obligations
axes.reason: All six are addressed and the brief remains bounded (916 whitespace-delimited words, seven findings), but obligations 2/3/5/6 contain material errors.

axes.label: consequential claims and full governing release/default/type/path conditions
axes.reason: Full primary-source claim checking completed; release, Linux path, historical suppression and refilter-phase defects prevent SourcePASS. Nonfatal API/type qualifications are retained.

axes.label: bounded useful discovery/negative/optional yield
axes.reason: Useful no-write/built-in-None/compatibility/stateful-filter leads; the no-errorlevel-change negative is false. Optional design remains bounded.

axes.label: wrong rejection/correction or unjustified universal abstention
axes.reason: False Linux refusal expectation and omitted-CLI classification constitute wrong rejection/correction risks. No unjustified universal abstention: a usable conditional policy is supplied.

axes.label: preservation/traceability/retained uncertainties and optional content
axes.reason: Final retains release/destination/concurrency/vendor/corpus limits and optional content with traceable source IDs; predecessor comparison is unavailable and was not attempted. Minor locator and hypothetical-example qualifications are recorded.

axes.label: proposed versus actually executed checks
axes.reason: Runtime regressions are explicitly proposed only; no runtime success is claimed. Reviewer reproduced hashes/static facts. Candidate execution provenance cannot be authenticated without excluded history/logs.

obligations.text: Identify the old concern, implementation/fix lineage, and released default relevant to 3.14.0.
obligations.reason: Historical concern, PEP/PR and default switch are correctly linked; released bytes take priority.

obligations.text: Bind omitted versus explicit filter and errorlevel behavior.
obligations.reason: Main 3.14 argument/attribute/default/threshold rules are sound; historical suppressed-error behavior and directory-fixup exception phase are wrong or unbound.

obligations.text: Separate file/link/path domains and destination assumptions.
obligations.reason: Strong link bases, containment and destination conditions; Linux absolute-member test and C:/ platform qualifier are deficient. Single-extract copy fallback also needs qualification.

obligations.text: State residual security and resource-exhaustion limits.
obligations.reason: DoS/resources/names/repeats/live-data limits and caller-owned controls are preserved; no claim of complete safety.

obligations.text: Avoid projecting an older issue onto every current code path.
obligations.reason: Read/write and archive-format separation are useful, but omitted 3.14 CLI is wrongly categorized as unfiltered.

obligations.text: Propose version-discriminating regression checks and conditional compatibility policy.
obligations.reason: Explicit data, feature detection and opt-in/fail-closed choices are appropriate; wrong absolute-path expectation and missed old/new suppression distinction undermine the matrix.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Release/platform/API binding and eight source hashes
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: The mapped files have the declared hashes; v3.14.0 exports extract/extractall with filter=None.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Stock CPython v3.14.0 on Linux; custom subclasses/vendor changes are outside the pinned implementation.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Explicit data/errorlevel=1/fresh destination plus limits is a bounded policy
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: Default errorlevel is 1; data_filter is a named/public function; documentation recommends fresh temporary directories, external limits and additional inspection.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Recommendation is sound for standard extractall and attacker-inert destination; limits and cleanup must be implemented by the caller, not provided by data_filter.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Old concern and CVE-2007-4559 motivation
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: PEP motivation describes unclear/incorrect prior inspection and malicious archive metadata; fully_trusted returns the member unchanged.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Historical unfiltered extraction; this does not establish vulnerability in every current API.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: PEP/issue/PR/default-change lineage
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: PEP metadata is Final/Python-Version 3.12. Issue 102950 tracks PEP 706 and links PR 102953; PR merged 2023-04-24T08:58:06Z at af530469954e8ad49f1e071ef31c844b9bfda414. Issue 121999 closed 2024-07-26T14:34:48Z and links PR 122002.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: JSON metadata/body establish implementation lineage, not all later fixes or comment discussions.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Omitted filter transitions from fully_trusted+warning to data
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: 3.12.3 returns fully_trusted_filter after a DeprecationWarning; 3.14.0 returns data_filter without warning. PEP describes the 3.12-3.13 transition; the 3.14 test asserts the data mock was called.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Both argument and extraction_filter must be None; non-None instance/class/subclass settings override omission. 3.13 history is checked against PEP, not a separately captured 3.13 runtime.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Named/callable filters and extraction_filter strings
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: Both release entry points have keyword-only filter. Explicit callables are returned directly; named strings index _NAMED_FILTERS; unknown hashable names raise ValueError; attribute strings raise TypeError when used.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Type errors/unhashable non-callable arguments are not covered by the unknown-string ValueError rule. Merely assigning a string does not raise until filter resolution.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: FilterError fatal/default abort; errorlevel=0 skip and 2 raises ExtractError
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: The primary member-filter phase leaves filtered=None on suppressed exceptions in 3.14 and skips. Fatal/nonfatal handlers raise above 0/1 respectively. Directory-fixup refilter catches _FILTER_ERRORS and continues regardless of errorlevel.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: The advertised fatal/abort rule needs the phase qualifier; custom/base FilterError does not necessarily carry tarinfo, unlike refusal subclasses.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: UnicodeEncodeError is newly handled as fatal
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: 3.14 catches UnicodeEncodeError in initial filtering and _extract_one; 3.12.3 catches OSError/FilterError in filtering and OSError in extraction.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Debug output is conditional on debug>=1; errorlevel does not suppress arbitrary exceptions/data-corruption errors.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Partial extraction and caller cleanup
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: extractall writes members as it proceeds and does not roll back; docs explicitly place cleanup on the caller.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Earlier text correctly requires cleanup on any abort; the abbreviated catch list in finding 6 should not be implemented as the sole cleanup boundary (e.g. ReadError also propagates).

consequential_claim_checks.claim: tar/data absolute member paths and containment
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: Filters strip leading slash/os.sep before isabs and realpath/commonpath checks. Linux /tmp/x becomes a relative member; the C:/foo surviving-absolute example is explicitly Windows-only. The released test expects stripped extraction on slash-based systems.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: After stripping, escape may still be rejected; not every originally absolute Linux name is refused. Member names and link targets have different rules.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: tar file/link domains
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: tar calls _get_filtered_attrs(...,False), so it checks member output paths but does not apply data's link-target checks.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: tar can create an outside-pointing link; a later member writing through it is rejected. 'tar ... blocks escapes' needs the write-path qualifier.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: data link rejection, normpath, relative bases
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: data refuses absolute/outside symlink and hardlink targets; symlinks are based at dest/dirname(name), hardlinks at dest. It sets normalized linkname while containment uses the original linkname during checking.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: normpath can change semantics when internal .. crosses symlinks; the docs explicitly warn. Inside-target links remain allowed, even when link creation is unsupported and copy fallback is used.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: data file-type refusal
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: For ordinary parsed archives, numeric mode is assigned and data's type branch accepts regular/hardlink/directory/symlink; FIFO/device/other nonaccepted types are refused.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Special-file rejection is inside if mode is not None. A supplied or modified TarInfo with mode=None bypasses this type branch; raw archive headers cannot encode None mode.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Mode and ownership sanitization
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: tar masks integer mode with 0755; data adds owner read/write, drops all execute bits without user execute, sets directory/symlink mode=None, and clears uid/gid/uname/gname.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: None metadata is intentionally preserved. Clearing ownership prevents archive-directed ownership changes; root may still call chown/lchown with -1 IDs, so 'skip chown' is a semantic shorthand, not no-syscall proof.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Live realpath, per-member filtering, directory refilter
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: 3.14 uses realpath(...,strict=os.path.ALLOW_MISSING), checks containment at each initial member, then re-filters unfiltered directories and lstat-checks them before metadata changes.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Missing paths are allowed during realpath; realpath/encoding errors can still propagate. Directory re-filter refusals are logged/skipped, not primary-member abort semantics.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Entry point/destination assumptions
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: extractall(path='.') and extract(path='') have different default spellings, both denoting the current directory; docs recommend a new temporary destination.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: A fresh directory does not replace exclusion of concurrent mutation; final retains attacker-inert/single-thread/no-concurrent-mutation conditions.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Residual DoS, names/sizes/counts, repeats/races/case shadowing
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: data_filter contains no such quotas/allowlists; the documentation lists these resource/name risks, duplicate overwrite semantics and live-data races.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: The list is expressly incomplete; OS limits remain necessary for work outside/preceding callbacks. Inside-target links are allowed.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: --filter-less CLI is an unfiltered old-warning path
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: 3.14 CLI forwards args.filter to extractall; without --filter it is None and the stock API resolves it to data_filter. PEP specifies this 3.14 CLI transition.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Only an older default or explicit fully_trusted/custom override yields that unfiltered classification; omitted CLI option is not such an override.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Read APIs are not filesystem extraction writes
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: extractfile builds a buffered archive reader or recursively resolves archive link targets; getmembers scans metadata, list prints, is_tarfile opens for reading.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Unsupported member types are also treated as regular by extractfile; links on nonseekable streams raise StreamError. Read-only does not mean immune to resource exhaustion.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: TarFile.add filter is a separate API
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: add uses a one-argument TarInfo filter while producing the archive; extraction filters take member and destination.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: A creation filter does not automatically validate later extraction.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: shutil tar defaults and ZIP filter failure
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: Released shutil tar unpack delegates filter=None to tar.extractall, hence stock 3.14 data default. Non-None filter is passed to built-in ZIP unpacker, whose signature has no filter; ZIP extract/extractall also have no filter parameter.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Built-in registered formats only; user-registered unpackers may implement other contracts. Candidate correctly records missing released shutil companion in its own corpus; this review supplements it.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: 3.14 LinkFallbackError and copy refilter
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: 3.14 defines LinkFallbackError and raises it when a fallback target filter raises _FILTER_ERRORS. extractall passes filter_function; extract does not forward it to _extract_one, so its copy fallback takes filtered=unfiltered.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Guard is conditional on API forwarding/filter presence and fallback needing an archive target. None-return skips the fallback copy. This qualifies a generic feature mention; final recommends extractall explicitly, so no separate categorical wrong claim is forced.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Feature detection, conditional compatibility, global setting
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: PEP/docs support hasattr(data_filter), fail-closed or explicitly acknowledged legacy fallback, callable extraction_filter, and restricting global changes to app/site with staticmethod.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Feature detection establishes API availability, not equivalence of older patched filtering implementations to v3.14.0. An absent API cannot receive filter='fully_trusted'; opting into old behavior means invoking that older API deliberately.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Stateful wrapper and optional context-manager opportunity
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: Docs show a stateful callback/context manager; tests demonstrate delegation to data_filter. Extending this to quotas/name rules is a proposed design.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Callback may be invoked again for directory fixup and fallback; counters must define accounting/idempotence. Docs illustration itself only counts callbacks, not a complete byte/name cap implementation.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Regression matrix is proposed and version discriminating
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: Omitted-filter/explicit-filter/name/attribute/errorlevel/link/type/mode/default cases correspond to released branches and tests; Linux absolute-member refusal expectation contradicts those branches.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Future device creation requires OS support/privilege; hardlink success needs a resolvable target; tar write containment differs from link-target acceptance. Checks must cover phases and releases rather than infer that all suppressed errors are equivalent.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Built-in filters never return None
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: fully_trusted returns member; tar/data return original or member.replace; all may raise instead.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Custom filters may return None; machinery may skip on suppressed errors without a built-in None return.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: No errorlevel semantics change from 3.12.3 beyond UnicodeEncodeError and directory refilter
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: 3.12.3 initializes tarinfo to the original member, then a failed filter assignment leaves it unchanged if the error is suppressed; 3.14 initializes filtered=None and skips. Suppressed ExtractError at errorlevel=1 likewise differs.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: This difference concerns initial member-filter exceptions, not just handler threshold code. At errorlevel=1 FilterError aborts both releases, so the core recommendation still benefits.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Retained source/vendor uncertainties
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: Captured issue/PR JSON contains bodies/metadata but no comment-thread collection; PEP permits redistributor changes. Shutil file is not in required input list.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: No inference about all vendor releases, actual deployed sandbox, comments or candidate history is made.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Executed static checks versus proposed runtime checks
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: Final explicitly labels regression checks proposed/not executed and reports hash/static inspection only. This review reproduced frozen/source hashes and independently read the relevant primary facts.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Candidate historical command/read execution is not independently authenticated because logs/history are excluded. No claim of passed runtime regressions or archive extraction is present.

consequential_claim_checks.claim: Traceability and source identities
consequential_claim_checks.checked_source_fact: All eight source IDs, versions and abbreviated hashes correspond to the input map; primary locators permit inspection.
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Default-filter assertions are at tartest.py:755-757, beyond the candidate's 742-754 locator. The referenced sources/SOURCES_USED.md is outside permitted inputs and was not read; enough source identity remains inside final.

defects.description: Unqualified classification of a --filter-less CLI as unfiltered is false within the declared stock 3.14.0 scope.
defects.impact: Can reject or diagnose a current data-filtered entry point on the basis of an older default.
defects.required_correction: Bind the CLI default to release and extraction_filter configuration; stock 3.14 omitted --filter uses data.

defects.description: The Linux-scoped text omits the Windows condition for C:/ absolute-path refusal and proposes unconditional absolute member-path rejection under data.
evidence: tarnew:785-797 explicitly strips leading / before checking isabs; C:/ comment says Windows
tartest:3723-3737 expects stripped names on slash-based systems
defects.impact: A regression expecting refusal for Linux /tmp/x would fail correct stock behavior; wrong rejection conflates member names with absolute link targets.
defects.required_correction: Test stripped/contained Linux absolute member names separately from escaping names and absolute links; label surviving drive-absolute cases Windows-specific.

defects.description: The no-errorlevel-semantics-change negative is contradicted by the old/new initial member-filter control flow.
evidence: tarold:2306-2325 keeps original tarinfo after a filter raises; 2347-2357 suppresses at errorlevel=0
tarnew:2494-2503 initializes filtered=None and skips after suppression
defects.impact: Erases a consequential security difference: a rejected member may proceed unfiltered at 3.12.3/errorlevel=0 but is skipped at 3.14.0. Suppressed custom ExtractError at level 1 also differs.
defects.required_correction: Restrict invariant claims to handler thresholds and add old/new regression expectations for a raising filter under errorlevel=0 and custom ExtractError under 1.

defects.description: The all-FilterError/default-abort language is not conditioned on the initial member-filter phase, although the output also discusses directory refiltering.
evidence: tarnew:2431-2439 catches those errors during directory fixup, logs and continues without consulting errorlevel
tarnew:2493-2503 has distinct initial member handling
defects.impact: A caller or stateful wrapper could incorrectly rely on any post-extraction FilterError reaching its abort-and-wipe handler.
defects.required_correction: State that directory-fixup refusal suppresses metadata update and is not a primary-member abort; design stateful cap/error accounting and checks around callback phase.

qualifications.fact: Built-in refusal subclasses carry tarinfo; base/custom FilterError need not.
Keep cleanup on any extraction failure, including corruption exceptions, rather than only two named exception classes.
tar can permit links pointing outside; later write paths are checked. fully_trusted accepts metadata but does not guarantee OS link/device creation.
Type rejection is conditional on non-None mode; ordinary on-disk header mode is integer.
Ignored ownership does not prove absence of chown calls under root; the IDs become -1.
extractfile also returns an archive reader for unsupported types; nonseekable link reads can raise.

Copy fallback re-filtering is conditional on forwarding the filter; extractall does so but stock extract does not. Core policy explicitly chooses extractall, so this is not graded as a false guarantee it explicitly made.
Stateful caps must account for repeated directory/fallback callbacks; the docs' example counts callbacks and is not a ready-made quota implementation.
Default-filter mock assertions are at test_tarfile.py:755-757, outside the candidate's cited 742-754 range; external SOURCES_USED.md was not inspected.

limits: Not identity/method-blind: allowed paths expose control labels.
Only mapped original inputs, exact frozen final and two same-scope released public primary companions were read.
Issue/PR captures contain body/metadata, not comments or the complete PR diff.
No downloaded code execution, archive extraction, software install or runtime regression testing.
No comparison to predecessors, other arms or evaluator answer corpus; no cost/winner judgment.
PEP's 3.13/backport statements are historical design/source claims; stock 3.12.3 and 3.14.0 code control the concrete release comparison.

executed_by_reviewer: Native create_goal/get_goal activation recorded before source assessment.
Verified frozen final hash before reading it for assessment.
Recomputed SHA-256 of all eight original sources; all match.
Read original brief/map/manifest/final plus relevant primary source implementations, docs, tests and JSON lineage fields.
Captured released v3.14.0 shutil.py and zipfile/__init__.py for same-scope companion claims; recorded exact bytes/hashes/URLs and locators.
not_executed: Any archive extraction or downloaded source execution
